A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThermalGaussian and provide readable, matching main sections, figures, tables, and equations. Both end with references and contain no appendix or embedded supplement. The supplementary material cited by both versions, particularly v2's announced limitations appendix, is unavailable, limiting that part of the comparison.

before.justification: Tables 2–4 report original thermal and RGB reconstruction experiments on ten RGBT-Scenes scenes, including component ablations, training time, rendering speed, and storage measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports ThermoNeRF RGB reconstruction results in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same multimodal initialization, MFTG, MSMG, OMMG, thermal smoothing loss, and Gaussian-count-based regularization. The revised prose clarifies existing procedures without changing their steps or objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate thermal and RGB novel-view synthesis on the same ten RGBT-Scenes scenes. No dataset, represented environment, or task is added; the new ThermoNeRF RGB rows use existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds ThermoNeRF to the RGB comparison, which previously included only 3DGS alongside the proposed variants. ThermoNeRF already participated in the thermal comparison in Table 2, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported 30,000 training iterations, smoothing coefficient of 0.6, NVIDIA 3090, 640×480 resolution, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain unchanged. The revised training-time result does not establish a changed training budget or measurement protocol.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same component ablations, and Figure 7 retains the regularization-coefficient comparison and Gaussian-distribution visualization. Relabeling the smoothing row as +MI+Lsmooth clarifies the existing cumulative ablation rather than introducing another test.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds ThermoNeRF RGB results, with reported averages of 18.46 dB PSNR, 0.586 SSIM, and 0.303 LPIPS; existing rows remain unchanged. Table 4 changes MFTG training time from 491s+575s to 491s without explaining whether this corrects the value or changes time accounting. Table 2 and the remaining Table 4 measurements are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same Gaussian representation, projection, rendering, losses, and regularization definitions. Added explanations of thermal equilibrium introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: thermal 3D Gaussian splatting, joint RGB/thermal reconstruction, RGBT-Scenes, improved rendering quality, and approximately 90% lower storage requirements.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly distinguishes MFTG's training speed, MSMG+MR's storage efficiency, and OMMG's rendering quality. Section 6 replaces explicit future directions concerning super-resolution and dynamic thermal processes with a pointer to a limitations/future-work appendix. That appendix is absent, preventing assessment of whether those directions were relocated and how substantially the limitations discussion changed.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise to release code and data with a project-page address, adding an access pointer without establishing resource availability from the PDFs alone. Hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain essentially unchanged; the revised MFTG timing lacks an explanation of stage accounting.

R1.justification: V2 adds Yan et al. (2020a) on multi-view image retrieval and Wang et al. (2024a, 2024b) on geo-localization. These are limited citation additions; the substantive positioning relative to 3DGS, ThermoNeRF, and Thermal-NeRF remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized background and method clarifications, revises several sentences and the conclusion's closing statement, updates author attribution, and adds acknowledgments. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands to accommodate ThermoNeRF, and Table 4 receives formatting and row-label changes. Figure 2 clarifies Mix50 as Mix with beta=0.5, while Figures 5–6 identify the illustrated method as OMMG. The underlying figure images remain unchanged; conference headers, page numbers, and front-page formatting are added.

improvement.justification: The added ThermoNeRF RGB comparison and clearer figure labels improve comparative completeness and clarity. However, v2 removes the 575-second term from the unchanged two-stage MFTG method's reported training time and newly emphasizes its speed without explaining the revision. The referenced limitations appendix is also unavailable. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
